request: Make abandoning The New Blood (40729) clean up the previous attempt before reaccepting it.
findings: HandleQuestLogRemoveQuest removed quest status, objective data and source items, but did not own/cancel the ritual's SmartAI actors or timed lists. The direct personal actors summon further NPCs and a gameobject; the descendants outlive their immediate summoner.

Nearest-creature SmartAI searches did not distinguish personal actors from static copies or another player's attempt. This could start a timed list on an unowned actor that ordinary personal-summon cleanup would miss.

The map-1220 ritual also addresses static world-trigger 35845 fire markers. Their original positions are retained through temporary personal copies rather than modifying/despawning shared markers. Map 1502 has no static fire-marker rows in the inspected database.
RemoveActiveQuest is used for successful rewards too. The return-to-start behavior belongs only in the abandon handler; object disposal also runs on normal status removal.
implementation: A quest attempt owns a QuestObjectScope with owner GUID and registered object GUIDs. Objects hold weak references and children inherit the scope before InitSummon runs. Registration/cancellation use a mutex and atomic cancellation flag because descendants can remain on an old map after their owner transfers.
Only New Blood's player-summoned council actors and player-forcecast jailer in maps 1220/1502 activate this mechanism. Ordinary creatures, pets and unrelated quests keep their existing behavior.

Cancellation invalidates the scope before hiding/despawning registered creatures, deleting gameobjects and removing conversations. Remote-map survivors self-remove before their next AI/event update; no foreign map objects are accessed from the player's map thread. Expired parents cannot spawn new scoped descendants.

SmartAI selects the nearest matching actor within the same attempt and filters area/invoker targets to the owner or same-attempt objects. Implicit spell targets use the same restriction. This prevents static/other-attempt actors from continuing a cancelled ritual.

Abandon clears pending scenario 962, ritual channel 199966, arrival stun 204833, chains 196229 and blackout 199362. In the actual scenario-962 map-1522 instance it releases only the player's non-permanent intro binding and returns them beside the existing Ritssyn spawn in map 1502. It does not reset another player's instance or the later scenario 998.

Quest acceptance and explicit status NONE also cancel retained scopes. Normal quest reward cleans up objects without running the abandon-only return. Inventory, equipment, pets and unrelated auras are preserved by the new handlers.
validation: Test-NewBloodQuestCleanup.ps1 compiles extracted production WorldObject and Player methods. It exercises descendant cleanup after parent loss, portals/conversations, remote-map expiry, same-tick reaccept, other-player isolation, owner-only targeting, late summons, repeated cancellation, scope destruction, concurrent registration/cancellation, aura isolation and intro/later-scenario binding guards.
Test-QuestAttemptCleanup.ps1 passes against production quest-status removal and source-item cleanup.
Test-EyeQuestChain.ps1 passes after the shared delayed-event exporter boundary adjustment; existing quest-attempt delayed events remain unchanged.
runtime: Release worldserver is built into the canonical build-extractors/bin/Release directory. This change requires that executable, not a SQL reload. The server is not automatically started and no character DB rows are modified.
